key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than reduce reflection: they can also improve wetting, crystallinity, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texturing is a multifunctional design lever that can boost efficiency and device reliability in perovskite photovoltaics, as well as related optoelectronic devices.
method: Review of recently reported texture-enabled effects in perovskite-based solar cells
Focus on benefits beyond light management: wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and stability
Synthesizes findings across solar cells, with relevance to photodetectors and LEDs
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates a literature survey of recently reported studies rather than a single experimental dataset, summarizing qualitative and performance-related improvements.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on fabrication process, texture geometry, and material system, so scalable implementation and reproducibility need careful validation.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
